# Phase 0 results (generated by analysis/phase0.py)

Source: 600 items from 10 clean paper 2 runs (60 tickets), `data` branch at `da1d6ae`. Reference: deterministic score. Judge verdict: first vote.

## Confusion matrix

| | Judge PASS | Judge FAIL |
|---|---|---|
| Correct (498) | 435 | 63 |
| Wrong (102) | 84 | 18 |

TPR 0.873, TNR 0.176, TPR + TNR - 1 = 0.050. True pass rate 83.0%, judge pass rate 86.5%.

Applying the correction to the same items it was measured on gives 83.0%, which equals the true rate by algebra. It is not a result.

## The 600 items are not independent

66 distinct (ticket, action) pairs. 13 tickets are ever wrong. Judge errors fall on 19 tickets, 11 of them in every run.

## Repeat agreement

The two votes differ on 21 items (3.5%). Of the 158 items with at least one wrong vote, they differ on 21.

## Correcting on held-out tickets

2000 random splits: TPR and TNR measured on half the tickets (all 10 runs), the judge's pass rate corrected on the other half.

- Correction undefined (TPR + TNR <= 1): 670 splits (33.5%).
- Median error of the raw judge pass rate: 4.7 points.
- Median error of the corrected rate, where defined: 19.3 points.
- Corrected rate further from the truth than the raw rate: 92.8% of defined splits.
- TPR + TNR - 1 deciles: [-0.11, -0.064, -0.017, 0.024, 0.054, 0.08, 0.112, 0.148, 0.196].

## Does a 95% interval for one run contain the true rate?

200 splits. Each labels 30 tickets (all runs) and estimates one clean run on the other 30 tickets. Intervals use 2000 resamples.

| Interval | Splits with an estimate | Coverage of the true rate | Median width | Median share of resamples undefined or dropped |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ticket-level (this repo) | 128 of 200 | 96.1% | 100 points | 43.9% |
| judgy 0.1.0 (item-level, dropped silently) | 128 of 200 | 43.8% | 54 points | 3.1% |
